sources.summary: Validate Atom-set Selection and the spec Alias
sources.claim:
# Validate Atom-set Selection and the spec Alias

## Claim checked

ownership **and** Claim targeting produce their respective direct **and** recursive Atom sets, **and** the alias `spec` selects **only** Active RMED Subtree-targeting Atoms.

## Test case

construct Scope Unit `A`, its child Scope Unit `A_CHILD`, a sibling Scope Unit `B`, **and** nested Atom Collections inside `A`. use the following distinct source Atoms; an omitted target resolves **to** the current Scope Unit.

| Atom | Current Scope Unit | Placement | Claim Structural Entity | Content Role | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a` | `A` | directly under `A` | omitted | Requirement | Active |
| `b` | `A` | nested Atom Collection | omitted | Method | Active |
| `c` | `A_CHILD` | directly under `A_CHILD` | omitted | Evaluation | Active |
| `d` | `B` | directly under `B` | `A` | Requirement | Active |
| `e` | `B` | directly under `B` | `A_CHILD` | Requirement | Active |
| `f` | `A` | directly under `A` | `B` | Requirement | Active |
| `g` | `A` | Draft placement | `A` | Requirement | Draft |
| `h` | `A` | directly under `A` | `A` | Plan | Active |
| `i` | `A` | Archived placement | `A` | Delivery | Archived |

derive **all** four sets for `A` **and** the alias `spec`. repeat **after** moving `a` into a nested Atom Collection under `A` **and** changing **only** Local Tiers; repeat with `b` assigned **every** RMED Content Role while retaining its other properties. **then** omit `B` from the claimed-complete source frontier, treat an Epic as a Scope Unit, replace targeting with ownership, copy a selected Atom as new authority, use an unresolved structural target **or** cyclic ancestry, **or** register `spec` as a separate Entity.

## Acceptance criteria

the results **must** be:

| Selection | Members |
|---|---|
| Owned Atoms | `a, b, f, g, h, i` |
| Targeting Atoms | `a, b, d, g, h, i` |
| Subtree-owned Atoms | `a, b, c, f, g, h, i` |
| Subtree-targeting Atoms | `a, b, c, d, e, g, h, i` |
| `spec` alias | `a, b, c, d, e` |

collection nesting **and** tier-only changes **must not** alter those results. `spec` **must not** create a separate Entity, independently maintained Atom set, **or** source of authority. incoming `d` **and** `e` retain ownership under `B`; outgoing `f` remains owned by `A` **without** entering its Targeting Atoms **or** `spec`. incomplete source coverage, unresolved required bindings, cyclic ancestry, ownership/target substitution, **and** duplicate authority fail explicitly.

## Failure disposition

report the source Revision, selected Scope Unit, expected set, **and** exact missing, extra, duplicated, **or** unresolved member; do **not** silently return a complete result **or** rewrite source ownership.

issues.topic: Governed selection versus generic Terms Graph
issues.observation: The generic Terms Graph definition and hierarchy checks exist. Selection of a governed-only view, missing/conflicting definitions and per-edge source traceability are not one fully explicit view contract. No new Term identity axis is necessary.
issues.disposition: Reuse definitions and reconcile the missing selection/traceability checks, preserving unresolved definitions as diagnostics.

issues.topic: Term hierarchy reach beyond Entity referents
issues.observation: NARROWER_THAN is expressed through Entity classification, while Term names can name separate Action/Process targets. Extending this hierarchy to those targets is not licensed merely by a display request.
issues.disposition: Check the exact required Term-relation domain. Preserve the existing restriction or ask the Operator if a broadened signature is necessary; do not infer a new relation name.

issues.topic: General vocabulary and unresolved candidates lack explicit index authority
issues.observation: Ordinary English and Project-specific meaning are distinguished, but there is no complete explicit source-occurrence diagnostic index specification. Capitalization or DEPENDS_ON membership alone cannot prove a missing definition.
issues.disposition: Add only missing diagnostic selection and uncertainty rules; distinguish ordinary vocabulary, missing definition, conflicting definition and unresolved candidate. Do not invent graph edges.

issues.topic: Allowed-value admission is not instance assignment
issues.observation: E383 says colon must assign one allowed value; R1245/R1436 define allowed-value relation and E449 rejects treating admission as assignment.
issues.disposition: Reconcile E383 with the admission-only relation and qualified identity model, preserving independent Property cardinality.

issues.observation: Immediate bearer and qualified identity rules do not make every complete graph or composed view a tree. Full traceability and sharing must survive a hierarchy display. Actions/Processes must not become duplicate Entities.
issues.disposition: Reuse the existing identity/qualification model and fill only display-independent derivation/validation gaps; assess whether explicit cycle checks are required without inventing a universal-tree rule.

issues.topic: Subject relation graph ownership is unresolved
issues.observation: GOVERNS and Subject DEPENDS_ON have direct endpoint meanings, but their owner graph kind and complete metadata are not established by those Claims. The composite navigation Projection cannot itself silently become their owner.
issues.disposition: Resolve the required graph-qualified identity before claiming schema closure; ask the Operator if below 99%. Do not reintroduce an independently maintained Atom Subjects source graph.

issues.observation: There is one governed target per Atom, not one governing Atom per target. Existing projection rules reproduce direct references but need explicit all-selected-Atoms backlinks and no maintained inverse fields.
issues.disposition: Reconcile faithful reverse navigation, qualified identity, cardinality direction and missing/ambiguous target diagnostics. Preserve all sealed P980 direct-link decisions.

issues.topic: Composed paths are not authored edges
issues.observation: Generic DRY and graph ownership constraints exist; a complete composed view contract preserving source facts, inverse navigation and multi-hop paths is not explicit.
issues.disposition: Reuse the existing graph kinds and Projection model. Retain original graph-qualified relation identities, direction, source revision and path versus edge distinction; never infer Task prerequisites or Scope Unit dependencies from shared Subjects.

issues.topic: Legacy direct relation registrations have incomplete graph-qualified metadata
issues.observation: Several registrations state direction or ordering domain but do not by themselves resolve all R806 fields including one owning graph kind. A registry builder must report that gap rather than fill it by endpoint compatibility or matching names.
issues.disposition: Inventory the exact metadata required for the selected composed view and reuse linked authority. Ask when missing ownership cannot be resolved. Do not broaden lifecycle or endpoint domains solely to complete a view.

issues.topic: Requirement-only registry extraction conflicts with D-owned Carrier relations
issues.observation: M120 step 1 extracts each Relation Kind from governing Requirement authority, but Carrier relation authority is D. Omitting it or changing D to R for the registry would violate the accepted role boundary.
issues.disposition: Reconcile generic registry source-role eligibility while retaining D ownership of Carrier definitions. P1084 may consume these facts but does not independently rewrite M120.

issues.topic: Views must not conflate source authority, currentness or scope
issues.observation: General Projection authority, no blanket persisted frontier, exact traceability and scope-preserving selection must be composed carefully. A partial selected graph is not a complete empty graph; authority definitions need not consume Journals as model-fact sources.
issues.disposition: Declare selection and completeness boundaries for these views; distinguish declared input frontier from what must be persisted in each Carrier. Do not universalize this Task's RMEDO-only admission to every possible graph query.

issues.topic: Applicable Methodology retrieval is not general backlink navigation
issues.observation: M225 has a specific prerequisite-closure retrieval rule, whereas direct Subject DEPENDS_ON does not establish execution order. The new view must not silently adopt M225 as universal Atom dependency semantics.
issues.disposition: Record this as a read-only boundary, not a mandate to rewrite compilation/retrieval. Any operational M225 reclassification belongs to P985/P986 after fresh review and explicit source ownership transfer if necessary.

issues.topic: Generic view Carriers and persistent index placement
issues.observation: Generic regeneration rules exist, but exact new view Carrier representation/placement is not settled. D307 prohibits persistent Subjects indexes inside Applicable Methodology, not every diagnostic output everywhere. Tool-specific signature JSON layouts are not a generic graph format.
issues.disposition: Reuse D where sufficient; establish missing generic representation/traceability without publishing outputs, hard-coding arbitrary Tool formats, replacing methodology Atom files with JSON or blindly repealing D307.

issues.topic: Derivation workflows currently carried as M
issues.observation: Existing generator/author steps may be reusable Actions or Processes under the accepted role boundary. A Task must not force new procedures into M to satisfy an RMED quota.
issues.disposition: The source-assigned successor evaluates its complete Claim; retain or reclassify only with source-preserving lineage and the 99% gate. P985/P986 must consume accepted successor maps and not independently remigrate the same old source.

issues.disposition: Retire/replace temporal authority and the remaining R1363 link in P984. P992 performs actual later Core Carrier migration; other source owners preserve the approved flat representation.

ownership_policy: Each selected source has at most one reserved content mutation owner; assignment is not a mandate to rewrite coherent authority. Null means shared read-only context.

Successors may reuse all selected sources read-only. A later Task needing an unassigned or another owner's source must record a root-coordinated ownership transfer before editing; no duplicate independent mutation.
P985/P986 consume completed maps and do not independently repeat a view Task's changes. P980 owns only Operation composition/control-flow schema, not generic Subject links.
P984 owns mandatory temporal-authority retirement and R1363's retained temporal parent. P992 consumes the finished Core content frontier for later Carrier application.
P993/P994/P995 and remaining tier/Scope Unit Tasks own their separate Carrier populations and remain untouched.
P1085 validates/hands off; it has no blanket mutation ownership over P1079..1084 sources. Repairs return to the assigned owner or receive an explicit coordinated transfer.
